item.title: Conversion to university: We are waiting for release of government gazette – Abdul, YABATECH Rector
item.description: By Adesina Wahab The conversion of Yaba College of Technology, YABATECH, to the Federal University of Technology and Vocational Studies is being delayed because the Federal Government is yet to release the official gazette that would convey that, the Rector, Dr Ibraheem Abdul, has disclosed. He stated this on Friday while answering questions on the sideline of the press briefing to herald the 38th convocation ceremonies of the College. “We are pretty much on course to becoming a University. The bill has been passed by the National Assembly and it has been signed into law by President Bola Tinubu. At our end, we are adequately prepared. What remains now is for the official gazette to be released by the Federal Government. When that is done, the institutional evaluation will be conducted by the Federal Ministry of Education and then the National Universities Commission, NUC, would come and accredit our courses. “Indeed, this historic conversion reflects the growing recognition by the President and the larger society of the importance of technology-driven and Vocational education in addressing Nigeria’s human-capital and industrial development needs,” he said. As part of the convocation ceremonies, Dr Abdul said the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, the Minister of Finance, Mr Taiwo Oyedele and Mrs Itunu Omotayo would be conferred Fellowship of the College. Also, Lagos State Deputy Governor, Dr Kadri Hamzat, will deliver the convocation lecture titled ” From silos to synergy: Reimagining Nigeria’s tertiary education system for national transformation”. The event will be chaired by the Minister of State for Education, Prof.Suwaiba Ahmad. Giving a breakdown of the number of graduating students, the Rector said a total of 10,886 would be involved. Out of the figure, 361 are graduating with distinction, 3,160 earned upper credit pass, 5,696 are graduating with lower credit pass and 1,669 have pass grade. Abdul added that the College has continued to promote entrepreneurship as an essential component of its education philosophy and that the citing of the Folawiyo Entrepreneurship Centre in the College was a testament to that . item.title: Emefiele: Court admits Supreme Court judgment in alleged $4.5bn fraud trial
item.description: An Ikeja Special Offences Court on Friday admitted a certified copy of a Supreme Court judgment linking former CBN Governor, Godwin Emefiele, to forfeited properties. Justice Rahman Oshodi admitted the judgment as Exhibit L after overruling objections by Emefiele’s defence counsel. Emefiele is facing a 19-count charge bordering on alleged gratification, corrupt demands and abuse of office involving $4.5 billion and N2.8 billion. His co-defendant, Henry Omoile, is facing a three-count charge of alleged unlawful acceptance of gifts. Oshodi ruled that the certified true copy of the Supreme Court judgment was admissible as a public document. He said the fact that only the lead judgment was tendered did not render it incomplete or inadmissible. The judge also addressed concerns about the prosecution’s reliance on a civil judgment in the ongoing criminal trial. He, however, restricted its use to establishing what the Supreme Court had decided in the previous proceedings. He stressed that the judgment could not constitute evidence for or against any party in the ongoing trial. “It has been well settled that court judgments are only used when tendered in a trial to determine and confirm what was actually decided in the case. “They are not used as evidence given in them for or against any of the parties therein,” Oshodi said. The Director of Public Prosecutions of the Federation, Mr Rotimi Oyedepo (SAN), had tendered the document through EFCC investigator, Mr Alvan Gurumnaan. However, Emefiele’s lead counsel, Mr Ojo Olalekan (SAN), opposed its admissibility, arguing that only four justices signed the judgment. He maintained that Supreme Court decisions were ordinarily delivered by panels of five or seven justices. Ojo also argued that the judgment arose from non-conviction forfeiture proceedings and was irrelevant to the prosecution’s case. Counsel to Omoile, Mr Adeyinka Kotoye (SAN), aligned himself with the objections and urged the court to reject the document. Kotoye argued that admitting the judgment could undermine the principle of estoppel and the defendants’ presumption of innocence. He also questioned the prosecution’s decision to introduce the document after proceedings had begun. Responding, Oyedepo argued that the document was a duly certified Supreme Court decision admissible under Sections 102 and 104 of the Evidence Act. Following the ruling, Gurumnaan faced cross-examination by Emefiele’s counsel over his role in the investigation. The witness said he personally obtained statements, analysed bank statements and coordinated other members of the investigation team. He confirmed interviewing Zenith Bank Managing Director, Dr Ebenezer Onyeagwu, but could not immediately recall whether a statement was obtained. Gurumnaan said the investigation involved hundreds of interviews with CBN officials, commercial bank employees and personnel of other government agencies. item.title: Why I lied about having cancer – Blessing CEO
item.description: By Wasiu Rokibat Nigerian social media personality Blessing Okoro, popularly known as Blessing CEO, has sparked fresh reactions after admitting that she falsely claimed to have breast cancer which in turn led to financial assistance from members of the public. The relationship influencer made the revelation during an interview with social media activist Martins Vincent Otse, better known as VeryDarkMan. Speaking during the interview, Blessing explained that although medical examinations discovered a lump in her breast, the result showed that it was not cancerous. However, she admitted that she deliberately presented the condition as cancer to attract sympathy from fans. In her words, “I do not have cancer. I had gone for a check-up and they found a lump in my breast, but it was not cancerous. I took advantage of that and told the public that the lump was cancerous. I played an emotional game.” According to her, she initially suggested that she might sell some of her personal belongings, including her car and house, before members of the public encouraged her to share her bank details for financial assistance. Blessing also disclosed that donations began coming in from different individuals but stopped after VeryDarkMan publicly questioned her cancer claims and demanded evidence of her diagnosis. “People had empathy, I did not come out to beg for funds. I played an emotional game. I wanted funds but I didn’t come out directly to ask for funds. I started with pretending I wanted to sell my personal belongings, my house, my car; It was fans who reached out to me in my DM, asking me to put out my account number; that’s when I put out my account number.” “The donation was rolling in, until VeryDarkMan came and say you people cannot be donating money for Blessing when there is no evidence. Immediately, VeryDarkMan made that video, the donation stopped. I am not proud of what I did.” The confession has renewed public attention to the controversy, which began in March 2026 when the influencer announced that she had breast cancer and appealed for financial support. She had previously acknowledged receiving about N13 million in donations but maintained that there had been confusion surrounding her medical condition. The matter also attracted the attention of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), which arraigned her over alleged offences connected to the fundraising campaign. She pleaded not guilty to the charges. Vanguard News The post Why I lied about having cancer – Blessing CEO appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Jaji wins Zamfara APC rerun primary with 26,646 votes
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto The incumbent member representing Kaura Namoda/Birnin Magaji Federal Constituency of Zamfara State in the House of Representatives, Hon. Aminu Sani Jaji, has won the All Progressives Congress (APC) court-ordered fresh primary election with 26,646 votes. Jaji defeated two other aspirants in the rerun conducted on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, to reclaim the party’s ticket after his earlier nomination was nullified by the Federal High Court in Abuja. The Chairman of the APC Electoral Committee for the exercise, Hon. Kabiru Idris, announced the results at the Kaura Namoda Collation Centre after the conclusion of voting and collation across the two local government areas. According to the committee, the constituency had 42,266 registered APC members, out of whom 27,389 were accredited, while 27,359 votes were recorded as total votes cast. Jaji’s closest challenger, Hassan Umar Dangaladima, polled 713 votes, while the third contestant, Musa Zubairu, failed to secure any vote. A breakdown of the results showed that Jaji won in both local government areas, polling 14,264 votes in Kaura Namoda against Dangaladima’s 465, while Zubairu scored zero. In Birnin Magaji, Jaji secured 12,382 votes, compared with Dangaladima’s 248 votes, while Zubairu again failed to record any vote. Declaring the results, Idris said Jaji had satisfied the requirements of the law, the APC Constitution and the party’s guidelines governing primary elections. “Having satisfied the requirements of the law, the APC Constitution and guidelines, I hereby declare Hon. Aminu Sani Jaji the winner of the fresh primary election,” he announced. The rerun followed a legal challenge instituted by Dangaladima at the Federal High Court in Abuja against Jaji’s earlier emergence as the party’s candidate for the constituency. The court nullified the earlier nomination and directed the APC to conduct a fresh primary within two weeks. The party’s national leadership subsequently fixed November 11, 2026, for the exercise in compliance with the court’s directive. Jaji, who is associated with the political camp of the Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle, has now secured the party’s ticket through the court-ordered process. The outcome settles the party’s immediate nomination contest in the constituency ahead of the 2027 general elections, following the legal dispute over its earlier primary election. item.title: Nigeria XI vs Tanzania: Lookman, Akor lead Super Eagles attack
item.description: Super Eagles goalkeeper Stanley Nwabali, defender Calvin Bassey and forward Ademola Lookman are among the players expected to feature in Nigeria’s starting line-up for their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Tanzania. The official line-up also includes Benjamin Fredrick, Ola Aina, Abdullahi Bewene, Wilfred Ndidi, Alhassan Yusuf, Tochukwu Nnadi, Alex Iwobi and Akor Adams. Nigeria’s expected starting XI vs Tanzania Stanley Nwabali Calvin Bassey Benjamin Fredrick Ola Aina Abdullahi Bewene Wilfred Ndidi Alhassan Yusuf Tochukwu Nnadi Alex Iwobi Ademola Lookman Akor Adams Head coach Éric Chelle will be looking to guide Nigeria to victory as the three-time African champions seek to strengthen their chances of qualifying for the tournament. Nigeria head into the encounter under pressure following their disappointing 3-0 defeat to Guinea-Bissau in September, having previously opened their campaign with a 2-1 victory over Madagascar. The Super Eagles currently occupy second place in Group L with three points, while Guinea-Bissau lead with seven points. Nigeria will be without star striker Victor Osimhen, who is sidelined by a knee injury, leaving Lookman and Adams among the attacking options expected to shoulder the responsibility. Chelle will be keen to secure maximum points against Tanzania as Nigeria continue their qualification campaign. The return fixture is scheduled for November 17 in Zanzibar. item.title: Malaysia arrests 53 Nigerians over immigration offences
item.description: By Favour Ulebor & Agency Report No fewer than 53 Nigerians were among 112 undocumented African nationals arrested by Malaysian immigration authorities between January and October 31 over various immigration offences, Malaysian newspaper, Utusan Malaysia, has reported. The Nigerians recorded the highest number of arrests among the African nationals, followed by Uganda with 13, Kenya with 10 and Ghana with eight. The Director-General of Malaysia’s Immigration Department, Datuk Zakaria Shaaban, disclosed the figures in an interview with Utusan Malaysia, published on Friday. According to the report, other nationals arrested included Somalia (6), Tanzania (6), Senegal (4), Algeria (3), Burkina Faso (2), Togo (2) and The Gambia (2). One national each from Guinea, Zimbabwe and Libya was also arrested. Shaaban said the most common offence was entering or remaining in Malaysia without a valid pass or permit, contrary to Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63. He said 85 people were arrested for the offence, including 47 Nigerians. “The primary offence recorded is entering and remaining in the country without a valid pass or permit, under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63; this resulted in 85 arrests, 47 of which involved Nigerian nationals,” he said. The immigration chief said 23 others were arrested for overstaying their permitted period under Section 15(1)(c) of the same Act. He added that three people were detained for violating the conditions of their immigration passes under Regulation 39(b) of the Immigration Regulations 1963. One Nigerian was also arrested for allegedly possessing forged documents under Section 56(1)(l) of the Immigration Act. The authorities also arrested an Algerian employer under Section 55B of the Act for allegedly employing foreign workers without valid immigration passes. Shaaban said the enforcement operations were part of efforts to curb undocumented migration and prosecute employers who engage or accommodate foreign nationals without proper immigration documents. “These ongoing enforcement operations reflect the authorities’ steadfast commitment to curbing the presence of undocumented migrants and taking firm action against any employers who harbor or employ them,” he said. However, the report did not disclose the identities of the Nigerians arrested or the specific locations where the arrests were made. item.title: 2027: Wike Criticises Obi Over National Anthem Snub At NDC Lagos Town Hall Meeting
item.description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, has said that the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, demonstrated lawlessness and an intent to divide Nigeria by allegedly refusing to recite the official one. Wike made these remarks on Friday, during a stakeholders’ town hall meeting in Ogu-Bolo Local Government Area of Rivers State, organised under the banner of the Rainbow Coalition to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election bid and All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates. ﻿ Addressing traditional rulers, community leaders, youths, and party faithful, the FCT minister argued that a leader who disregards national symbols cannot be trusted with the presidency. “A whole national anthem of a country is being sung. A man who wants to be President of Nigeria would disobey and sit down. And then not only that, when a different national anthem that is not being used for Nigeria [was sung], he stood up. “In a way, he does not belong to this country. In a way, he has said he does not belong to this country; that if you give him the president, he would do a different thing that will divide Nigeria. “A man who does not believe in Nigeria, someone who derives joy in ridiculing the country by disrespecting its symbolic National Anthem must not be allowed to come near the presidency of our country,” the minister said. Wike further criticised Obi’s political trajectory and past governance record, alleging that the former Anambra State governor frequently abandons political parties whenever internal crises arise, rather than staying to resolve them. He also faulted Obi for not conducting local government elections during his eight-year tenure as governor, describing it as a contradiction to his professed belief in the rule of law. Tackles Atiku, Amaechi In addition to targeting Obi, the FCT Minister took aim at the opposition coalition involving former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and former Rivers State Governor Rotimi Amaechi. Wike questioned their track records in public office, specifically citing the state of seaports during Amaechi’s tenure as Minister of Transportation and alleging that the administration demolished Government Secondary School, Ogu, without rebuilding it, alongside unfulfilled promises regarding a 1,000-bed specialist hospital. Urging the people of Ogu-Bolo to disregard what he termed “big grammar” from opposition politicians on television, Wike maintained that President Bola Tinubu’s administration had delivered tangible dividends of democracy to the area. He pointed to the construction of the Ogu-Bolo Civic Centre—facilitated through the federal appointment of an indigene, Boma Iyaye—as well as the conduct of local government elections. He urged people in the area to massively support the re-election of Tinubu, Kingsley Chinda for Governor of Rivers State and all the APC candidates seeking National Assembly seats. item.title: 10 footballers with the most red cards in football history
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Footballers are often praised for keeping their cool when the stakes are high, but some of the game’s most recognisable names have become known for receiving repeated red cards. From tough-tackling defenders to forceful midfielders, their careers have combined success on the pitch with frequent disciplinary woes. Gerardo Bedoya stands clear at the top of the ranking, with 46 red cards during his playing career and recognised by the Guinness World Records. The former Colombia international’s fiery reputation followed him into coaching: in 2016, he was sent off just 21 minutes into his first match as an assistant coach at Santa Fe. Red-card totals can differ between databases because no single global record tracks every player’s dismissals across all competitions. According to a recent ranking by Planet Football, here are the 10 players who have been sent off the most times in football history. Alexis Ruano Delgado — 22 red cards The Spanish centre-back played for Málaga, Getafe, Valencia and Sevilla, among other clubs. He won the Copa del Rey with Valencia in 2008. Rafael Márquez — 22 red cards The Mexican defender played for Barcelona, Monaco and New York Red Bulls, among other clubs, and represented Mexico at five World Cups. Six of his red cards came during his time at Barcelona. Cyril Rool — 22 red cards The French midfielder played in Ligue 1 for clubs including Lens, Bordeaux and Nice. His career, which ran from 1993 to 2010, also included more than 150 yellow cards. Gerardo Torrado — 22 red cards Mexico’s former defensive midfielder earned 144 international caps and played at three World Cups. He spent 11 years at Cruz Azul, where he was sent off 14 times. Paolo Montero — 23 red cards The Uruguayan defender played for Atalanta and Juventus, winning Serie A titles with the Turin club. Sixteen of his 23 dismissals came in Italy’s top flight, where he holds the league record, according to the ranking. Edgar Davids — 25 red cards The Dutch midfielder won the Champions League with Ajax and also played for Juventus and Tottenham. Known for his energetic style, he continued his career with Barnet in England’s lower leagues. Felipe Melo — 26 red cards The Brazilian midfielder and defender played for clubs including Juventus, Inter, Galatasaray, Palmeiras and Fluminense. He retired in 2024, aged 41, after a career spanning more than two decades. Pablo Alfaro — 27 red cards The Spanish centre-back played for Barcelona, Atlético Madrid, Racing Santander and Sevilla. He was part of Barcelona’s 1992–93 La Liga-winning squad and later earned a UEFA Cup winner’s medal with Sevilla. Sergio Ramos — 30 red cards The World Cup winner and former Real Madrid captain is second, with 30 career dismissals. His total includes 26 red cards at Real Madrid and four across spells with Sevilla, Paris Saint-Germain and Monterrey. item.title: NIS moves to prevent foreign interference in 2027 elections
item.description: The Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) and other stakeholders have convened to strategise measures to prevent interference by foreign elements in the upcoming 2027 general elections. The NIS, the Department of State Services (DSS), the Border Communities Development Agency (BCDA) and other stakeholders convened at a sensitisation workshop at the NIS headquarters on Friday in Abuja. The workshop is themed: “The Role of the Nigeria Immigration Service in Election Monitoring and Management.” Speaking at the workshop, the NIS Comptroller-General, Mrs Kemi Nandap, said that the successful conduct of the upcoming elections required institutional cooperation from all security stakeholders. Nandap, represented by the Deputy Comptroller-General in charge of Visa and Residency, Mrs Franca Nwanneka, said that the deliberation was important as the general election is fast approaching. “Beyond the responsibility of conducting credible elections, there is the equally important task of providing a peaceful and secure environment in which the democratic process can thrive. “Achieving this requires collective vigilance, effective coordination and the commitment of all institutions entrusted with safeguarding our nation,” she said. According to her, the NIS occupied a strategic position in the nation’s security architecture as the agency saddled with the responsibility and mandate of border security and migration management. “We must therefore remain alert to the influx of foreigners, emerging threats, particularly irregular migration and smuggling of migrants. “We must also be on high alert to trafficking in persons and other transnational criminal activities capable of undermining national security,” she said. Nandap also reaffirmed the NIS’ stance as a non-partisan service loyal to the Constitution and the Federal Republic of Nigeria, and warned officers against using official capabilities to participate in politics. She charged officers to demonstrate the highest standards of political neutrality, discipline and respect for the rule of law. The CG charged senior officers, zonal coordinators, comptrollers, and heads of formations to ensure that every command is adequately prepared before, during and after the elections. She emphasised strengthened surveillance, intelligence gathering, effective deployment and close coordination with relevant security agencies as key areas that could facilitate credible elections. “No single agency can address the complex security challenges confronting our nation in isolation. Our collective strength lies in our ability to work together, share timely information and respond decisively to emerging threats. “I look forward to even stronger collaboration as we approach the elections because the task of securing our nation and sustaining public confidence in our institutions is a collective responsibility,” she added. item.title: 2027: Adebutu hails court ruling, says justice has prevailed
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State for the 2027 election, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, has hailed the judgment of the Federal High Court, Abuja, directing the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to restore his name to the list of candidates for the forthcoming governorship election within 24 hours. Adebutu described the judgment, delivered by Justice Peter Lifu on Friday, as a victory for justice, the rule of law and democratic principles. Reacting to the ruling in a statement, the PDP chieftain declared: “Justice has prevailed! Relief is here!” He described the judgment as a significant development in the legal battle over his exclusion from INEC’s published list of candidates for the 2027 Ogun State governorship election. Adebutu said he had consistently maintained that his PDP membership, registration and emergence as the party’s governorship candidate were legitimate and in accordance with due process. “From the moment my name was omitted from INEC’s published list, I maintained that the facts surrounding my PDP membership, registration and the process that produced me as the party’s governorship candidate were clear,” he said. According to him, the party remained confident in the strength of its position and resolved to pursue the matter through the appropriate legal channels. He noted that the judgment had reaffirmed the importance of due process, stressing that political and electoral disputes should be determined on their merits rather than on speculation or premature conclusions. Adebutu expressed appreciation to the national leadership of the PDP, particularly Chief Nyesom Wike, whom he described as the party’s national leader, and its National Chairman, Hon. Abdulrahman Mohammed, for their support and confidence throughout the legal proceedings. He also thanked the Ogun State PDP leadership, party members, supporters and residents of the state for their solidarity during the period of uncertainty. “I am equally grateful to the Ogun State PDP leadership, our members, supporters and the good people of Ogun State who remained steadfast. Your patience, encouragement and confidence have been invaluable,” he stated. The governorship candidate also commended the judiciary for its role in upholding justice, emphasising that democratic institutions must remain independent and impartial, irrespective of political interests or affiliations. “Our democratic institutions must remain strong, independent and committed to upholding the law, regardless of political interests or affiliations,” he said. Welcoming the judgment, Adebutu said his focus remained on addressing the developmental challenges confronting Ogun State and engaging residents on practical solutions to improve their welfare. item.title: Carrick says ‘love never dies’ after Man Utd sacking
item.description: Michael Carrick wished Manchester United “nothing but success” 24 hours after he was sacked, reaffirming his enduring love for the club, who have already appointed Mauricio Pochettino as his replacement. Carrick impressed after taking over as interim boss following Ruben Amorim’s acrimonious exit in January, leading United to Champions League qualification. He was rewarded with a two-year permanent deal, but results have nose-dived in this campaign. The Red Devils are in the Premier League relegation zone after winning just one of their 10 league matches so far. The Old Trafford club named former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain boss Pochettino, currently USA head coach, as their new manager on Friday. Despite the downturn this season, Carrick remained popular with supporters in part for his role as a player in multiple triumphs under Alex Ferguson, who retired in 2013. The 45-year-old said his affection remained rock-solid. “I want nothing but success for Manchester United. This club has been such a big part of my life and that will never change,” Carrick wrote in an Instagram post. “I’ll always be proud to have played my part and I’ll always want the very best for it. “I’ll be right there with you from now on, watching from the sidelines, cheering the lads on.” The former England midfielder paid tribute to the fans, his coaching staff and United’s players. “I’ve had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love,” he wrote. “There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I’m incredibly grateful. With that comes huge responsibility, and to be at Manchester United, you need to understand exactly what that means. “It’s different to anywhere else. Ultimately, you need to push to be the best, but there is a culture, there are values and there are behaviours that you have to live by and respect, which have been built over a long period of time. “It’s a football club that is unique, with substance and history that cannot be ignored. This is what inspired me every single day.” Carrick described United’s fans as a “special, rare breed”. “We’ve had some great times this year and moments we’ll all remember,” he said. “The best thing about being in my position was seeing so many of you lose yourselves in the emotion of those moments, leaving the stadium desperate to come back again next time. “I just wanted to give you something back. item.title: FG Signs Port Harcourt Airport Concession Agreement, Assures Workers’ Protection
item.description: The Federal Government has signed a concession agreement for the Jeremiah Obafemi Awolowo International Airport, Port Harcourt, with PH Airport Limited, following assurances from the concessionaire that the arrangement would not lead to job losses. The agreement was signed at the office of the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, in Abuja, on Thursday. The Federal Government delegation was led by Keyamo, while PH Airport Limited was represented by its Group Managing Director, Eyo Asuquo. The signing followed a meeting between the minister and aviation union leaders to discuss the implications of the concession for airport workers. Speaking on behalf of the unions, Comrade Ben Nnabue said organised labour had approved the agreement after receiving assurances that no aviation worker would lose their job as a result of the arrangement. He said job security remained a major concern for the unions and that they were satisfied with the commitments made before endorsing the agreement. Photo of the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, and the federal government delegation in Abuja, on Thursday. Also speaking, Asuquo highlighted Port Harcourt’s strategic importance in the Gulf of Guinea, describing the airport as a potential gateway for regional commerce, investment and connectivity. He said PH Airport Limited intended to improve the airport’s infrastructure and operational standards, adding that the concession would create more employment opportunities rather than result in job losses. According to him, the company’s vision extends beyond managing the facility to expanding airport-related activities, attracting investment and unlocking its economic potential. The Director-General of the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, Chris Najomo; Managing Director of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, Olubunmi Kuku; ministry directors and aviation union leaders attended the event. The concession agreement was subsequently signed by the concessionaire and relevant ministry officials, with Keyamo presiding over the ceremony. The Federal Government said the agreement was part of its broader efforts to attract private-sector investment and expertise into the development and management of Nigeria’s airport infrastructure. Under President Bola Tinubu’s administration, the Ministry of Aviation and Aerospace Development has pursued reforms aimed at modernising airports, improving operational efficiency and strengthening the aviation sector’s contribution to economic growth. The Port Harcourt airport concession is expected to improve the passenger experience, strengthen airport services, and attract investment to the facility. item.title: Obi condemns attack on NDC supporters in Lagos, urges peaceful defence of votes
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has condemned the attack on the party’s supporters at a town hall meeting in Lagos on Thursday, urging them to remain peaceful while defending their democratic rights. Obi made the call in a statement posted on his X handle on Friday, a day after suspected thugs disrupted the party’s gathering in Oregun, Lagos. He said he had been informed that a group of thugs mobilised to attack participants who arrived early for the meeting, noting that he had travelled to Lagos from Abuja to attend a commendation service for Chief Sir Okey Ezibe before proceeding to join supporters at the town hall meeting. “The political violence being enabled by certain political actors against our supporters is an ill wind that blows no one any good. Anarchy consumes everyone,” he said. “We will remain law-abiding, even in the face of extreme provocation.” Obi said the town hall meeting went ahead despite the disruption and participants raised concerns about reviving the economy, the high cost of living, corruption, insecurity, support for vulnerable citizens and the integrity of elections. He said the first responsibility of any government was to secure the country and unite its people around a shared purpose. He also pledged that his administration would pursue policies to reduce living costs, improve welfare and invest in healthcare and education. On the forthcoming elections, the former Anambra governor said protecting the integrity of the process was a shared responsibility, saying the NDC would deploy agents to polling units to observe and document voting, ward collation and the final declaration of results. “I encouraged our people to eschew violence while remaining peaceful, vigilant, and resolute in defending their democratic rights,” he said. Vanguard reported that suspected political thugs armed with cutlasses, cudgels and stones invaded the Oregun rally on Thursday, attacking supporters and injuring some participants, although Obi was not at the rally when the incident occurred. item.title: Muniz answers Murphy in three minutes as Fulham hold Newcastle
item.description: Newcastle spent most of Saturday afternoon looking for an opening at Craven Cottage. When Jacob Murphy finally curled the ball past Bernd Leno in the 80th minute, the visitors had a lead that lasted only 179 seconds. Rodrigo Muniz equalised for Fulham in the 83rd, leaving the sides with a 1-1 draw on 7 November 2026. Iwobi and Calvin Bassey both started for Fulham. The match went into the break goalless, a result that has to be kept separate from the full-time draw at betting sites in Cameroon , since the two selections cover different periods. item.description: Twenty-five years after Michael Owen won it, the men’s Ballon d’Or belongs to an Englishman again. Harry Kane picked up the 2026 award at the London Palladium on 26 October, with 73 goals behind his claim. Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé finished second. Kane also left the ceremony with the Gerd Müller Trophy for the leading men’s goalscorer. The national side finished third, its best placing since the 1966 victory. The remaining international goals in his season record came in qualifying and friendlies. Five came in five World Cup qualifiers, with another in two international friendly appearances, giving him 12 goals in 14 England outings overall. Bayern’s three domestic trophies give the goals some context, too. They kept the league title and lifted the DFB-Pokal, after winning the Franz Beckenbauer Supercup. The Ballon d’Or case included a team collecting silverware while Kane supplied the finishing. Owen’s wait ends, and Bayern’s too Kane becomes the fifth English player to receive the Ballon d’Or. The four names before him cover very different chapters of the award: 1956: Stanley Matthews took the first award. 1966: Bobby Charlton added it to his World Cup year. 1978 and 1979: Kevin Keegan won twice with Hamburg. 2001: Michael Owen brought it to Liverpool. Owen’s victory had remained the last English success for a quarter of a century. Kane’s award adds another name to that short list rather than another win for a previous recipient. item.title: Yiaga Africa: Youth participation in 2027 elections declines by 20%
item.description: Yiaga Africa, an NGO, says the number of young people under 35 expected to participate in the forthcoming general elections has declined by a further 20 per cent, in spite of the enactment of the Not Too Young to Run law. The Executive Director, Yiaga Africa, Dr Samson Itodo, made this known at the Ready To Run Bootcamp for young candidates of political parties under the age of 35 years in Lagos on Friday. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that the programme, which is funded by the European Union, has the theme: “Ready to Run Bootcamp: From Aspiration to Representation”. Itodo, represented by its Programme Coordinator, Mr Ibrahim Faruk, said that following the passage of the law in 2019 by President Muhammadu Buhari, young people under 35 constituted 38 per cent of candidates in the 2019 general elections The executive director said that the percentage further dropped to about 28 per cent in 2023. Itodo attributed the decline to the high costs for nomination forms, campaigning, along with party structures and primary control among others. The executive director added that this leaned toward established interests, which had pushed young people to the margins and made securing political tickets difficult. He said: “The first thing Yiaga is doing is what we are doing here today, you know, there is the narrative that says young people are not ready to run. “Yiaga Africa is also changing that narrative to say young people are ready to run, and we are doing that through the Ready to Run boot camps to ensure that young people are ready to run. “​We have also done a lot of electoral reform advocacy; a lot of the changes to the Electoral Act have been as a result of advocacy. ​”While there have been attempts to reduce the high cost of nominations, also ensure that parties are more democratic and inclusive in a way that supports young people. “​Some of these advocacy efforts have been fruitful, some of them have taught us lessons. “We will continue to advocate for an electoral process that accommodates more young people, is more inclusive, less expensive and as democratic as possible,” he said. ​Itodo urged INEC and stakeholders to emphasise on ensuring a credible, secure, and logistically sound electoral process that the outcomes would reflect the will of the people. He also urged young Nigerians to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), participate fully and peacefully as voters, candidates, or agents, and refuse to sit out the democratic process. In his remarks, the Founder, African Governance Institute for Development, Mr Seyi Adisa admitted that running for office was more difficult for young people, as elections required not only financial resources but also “social capital”. According to him, while older individuals generally have more experience and social capital, young people can win elections. “It is more difficult, but achievable with the right strategies, networks, coalitions, and alliances,”he said. item.title: Ebola: Nigeria records zero secondary infections as 62 contacts exit monitoring
item.description: … Index patient recovers, discharged in Switzerland By Chioma Obinna Nigeria has recorded zero secondary transmission of the deadly Bundibugyo Virus Disease, a form of Ebola, following the successful completion of the 21-day monitoring period for all 62 contacts linked to the imported case confirmed in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) on October 20, 2026. The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) yesterday announced that the last contact had been discharged from monitoring, with none of the 62 individuals developing the disease. In another development, the index patient, who was medically evacuated to Switzerland on October 26 for further treatment, has recovered, subsequently tested negative for the virus and been discharged from hospital. However, the NCDC warned that the successful completion of contact monitoring does not amount to a formal declaration that the outbreak is over, insisting that Nigeria must sustain heightened surveillance amid continued Ebola transmission in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). Director-General of NCDC, Dr Jide Idris, who announced the development, described the outcome as encouraging, crediting early detection, prompt investigation and cooperation between health authorities and affected communities. “The 21-day monitoring period for contacts linked to the index case has been completed, with the last contact discharged today. We are glad to announce that none of the contacts became ill with the disease, meaning no transmission from the index case,” Idris said. He disclosed that 13 of the 62 contacts reported fever or other non-specific symptoms during the monitoring period. All 13 were tested for Bundibugyo Virus Disease and returned negative results. Similarly, seven alerts reported in Adamawa, Rivers, Borno, Lagos and Ekiti states within the last three weeks were investigated, with laboratory tests confirming that none was positive for the virus. The NCDC boss explained that the imported case was detected following an alert raised by healthcare workers through the agency’s event-based surveillance system, enabling the government to activate an emergency response and commence investigations. Under the leadership of the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate, the National Emergency Operations Centre was activated, while an Incident Management System was established to coordinate the response. According to Idris, the response focused on providing clinical care, identifying and monitoring exposed persons, preventing further transmission, protecting healthcare workers and strengthening disease surveillance. He said contact tracing covered healthcare facilities, households and other relevant settings, while infection prevention and control measures were reinforced in health facilities within the FCT and across the country. item.title: 2027: Obanikoro confident of Tinubu, Hamzat’s victory
item.description: Sen. Musiliu Obanikoro, a chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), has expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu and the party’s governorship candidate in Lagos State, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, will emerge victorious in the 2027 general elections. Obanikoro, Director-General, PBAT-KOH Campaign Council, Lagos State, gave the expressed this while speaking during the Lagos SWAGA 2.0 Summit and launch in Lagos, on Friday. He said the party was well positioned to win Lagos, adding that the achievements of the Tinubu administration at the federal level and those of the Lagos State Government had endeared the APC to the electorate. “We are confident of victory. President Tinubu has shown leadership, and Hamzat has the experience and capacity to sustain the progress of Lagos. “Lagos residents know what good governance looks like, and they will not gamble with their future “I commend the grassroots mobilisation and initiative of SWAGA 2.0 for mobilising supporters to this event venue. “With this great turnout, massive victory is assured for Tinubu and APC gubernatorial candidate, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, ” he said. Obanikoro tasked party members to intensify grassroots mobilisation and ensure the party delivered 3.5 million votes for Tinubu and Hamzat in the state He said the target was achievable if members remained united, disciplined and committed to the party’s campaign structure. “Our target is 3.5 million votes. It is not just a number, it is a statement that Lagos stands firmly behind Tinubu and Hamzat,” he said. He urged party leaders at ward and local government levels to take the campaign to every polling unit and engage voters on the party’s achievements. Obanikoro said the opposition lacked the structure and credibility to challenge the APC in Lagos, describing the party as the only party with a clear vision for the state and the country. He called on supporters to shun violence and conduct issue-based campaigns, stressing that the APC would win through performance, not intimidation. “We must campaign with our records. We must not engage in violence. Our victory will come from the people because they have seen what we have done,” he said. He assured supporters that the party leadership would provide the necessary support to ensure a hitch-free campaign and victory at the polls. item.title: 95,000 PVCs uncollected in Plateau – INEC
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), says more 95,000 Permanent Voters Cards (PVCs) have not been collected in Plateau. Prof. Samuel Egwu, the Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in the state, disclosed this during a press conference on Friday in Jos. The REC explained that the uncollected PVCs were largely for those who registered before the 2023 general elections. Egwu, who said that the commission was worried over the large number of unclaimed PVCs in the state, urged voters to take advantage of the ongoing distribution exercise to collect their PVCs. “More than 95,000 PVCs from 2023 were still with our Electoral Officers across the state. “We call on who those who registered before the last general elections to come and collect their PVCs to enable them participate in the 2027 general elections,”he advised. The REC said that PVCs from the first phase of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) exercise conducted between August and December 2025, were made available for collection at INEC offices across the 17 Local Government Areas (LGAs) of the state. He said particularly that the PVCs of Shendam, Langtang North, Jos South and Kanam, were now available for collection. “More than 19,000 PVCs for those who applied for transfers and corrections are also available for collection. “All PVCs for the second phase of CVR conducted between January and April, are available and have been taken to the 17 LGAs for collection. “PVCs for the third phase of CVR are not ready, but will be made available before the end of November for collection,”he said. Egwu also disclosed that all non-sensitive materials for the 2027 general elections were available at the INEC office in Jos and would soon be distributed to the 17 LGAs. He further said that training of electoral officers who were not trained in 2023 had commenced. The REC reiterated INEC’s readiness to conduct a credible election in 2027. item.title: COREN Commends Nile university as 261 Engineering graduates take professional oath
item.description: Nile University of Nigeria has inducted 261 graduates of its Faculty of Engineering into the Nigerian Society of Engineers (NSE) and administered the Council for the Regulation of Engineering in Nigeria (COREN) oath in its maiden Induction and Oath-Taking Ceremony, as the institution intensifies efforts to align its programmes with international standards. The ceremony marks a significant milestone for the University’s Faculty of Engineering, which was established in 2009 and has grown into one of its flagship academic units, offering programmes in Civil Engineering, Computer Engineering, Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, and Petroleum and Gas Engineering. Prof. Prema A. Kirubakaran, who represented the Vice-Chancellor, described the ceremony as a landmark achievement for the Faculty and urged the newly inducted engineers to uphold the values of integrity, responsibility and continuous learning throughout their careers. Delivering the keynote address, Engr. Dr. Adamu Muhammed, MNSE, MNSChE, PMP, AMIChemE, Terminal Manager, NNPC Limited, praised Nile University of Nigeria for its contribution to engineering education, describing the institution as one capable of standing alongside leading universities globally. He challenged the new engineers to remain honest, continue learning and apply their knowledge to solving Nigeria’s developmental challenges. He urged the graduates to build careers defined by innovation, discipline and professional excellence. Speaking at the ceremony, Engr. Prof. Okorie Austine Uchegbusi Uche, FNSE, Registrar of COREN, commended Nile University of Nigeria for its implementation of Outcome-Based Education (OBE), describing it as one of the few institutions in the country actively applying the approach, which emphasises measurable competencies and graduate outcomes. Reflecting on the significance of the occasion, the Dean of the Faculty of Engineering, Engr. Prof. Abdulhameed Danjuma Mambo, said the induction signified the graduates’ readiness to assume the responsibilities of professional engineering practice. “Graduation shows that you have learned, but induction shows that you have become a professional,” he said. According to him, while members of the public may never see the calculations behind engineering projects, they place their trust in the professionalism and judgment of engineers responsible for them. Prof. Mambo said the Faculty remains committed to producing graduates equipped with the technical knowledge, professional values and practical skills required to contribute to national development. He noted that the ongoing accreditation activities involving the Faculty form part of efforts to ensure that its programmes meet global standards and remain competitive internationally. item.title: Is Galadima the Round Peg in the Round Hole for Adamawa?
item.description: In Nigerian politics, the phrase “a round peg in a round hole” is often used to suggest that a candidate’s temperament, experience and timing align perfectly with the demands of the moment. In Adamawa State, that description is increasingly being attached to Ahmed Tijjani Galadima, the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate for 2027. But is he truly the right fit for Adamawa’s complex political and developmental realities, or simply the beneficiary of strategic party consensus? Adamawa is no ordinary political battleground. Situated in Nigeria’s North-East, the state has long balanced agricultural potential with security challenges, urban expansion with rural neglect, and a politically vibrant electorate with shifting party loyalties. Governorship contests here are rarely predictable. Personal networks, regional considerations, grassroots mobilisation and elite consensus all play decisive roles—and often collide. Galadima’s emergence as the APC’s standard-bearer was no accident. A seasoned technocrat, he previously served as Executive Secretary of the Petroleum Technology Development Fund (PTDF), a position that placed him at the intersection of public administration, human capital development and federal policymaking. Within policy circles, that experience is often cited as evidence of administrative competence—a quality many voters say has become increasingly important after years of governance characterised more by political brinkmanship than institutional reform. Within the APC, his candidacy also represents consolidation. Several key aspirants stepped aside before and during the primary process, sparing the party the bruising internal contest that has weakened it in previous election cycles. For a party seeking to reclaim power in Adamawa from the administration of Governor Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri, unity is more than desirable; it is essential. Galadima’s ability to attract support across competing blocs suggests he enjoys both political goodwill and strategic alliances. Yet politics in Adamawa extends beyond party arithmetic. The electorate remains deeply concerned about security, particularly in communities affected by the spillover of insurgency in the North-East. Farmers want safer farmlands, traders need secure transport corridors, and young people seek economic opportunities that do not require leaving the state. Any candidate seeking to be regarded as the “right fit” must present credible solutions to these interconnected challenges. Supporters argue that Galadima’s administrative experience positions him to drive economic renewal. Adamawa’s economy remains largely agrarian, with significant untapped potential in agro-processing, livestock production and cross-border trade with neighbouring Cameroon. With improved infrastructure, targeted investment incentives and better access to rural finance, the state could move beyond subsistence agriculture towards value-added production. item.title: Violent campaigns
item.description: Barely two months to the 2027 general elections, there are rising cases of political violence across Nigeria, despite efforts by various bodies to discourage mayhem before, during and after the polls. The presidential and National Assembly elections are scheduled to hold on January 16, 2027, while the governorship and State Assembly elections have been slated for February 6, 2026. In the last seven days, there have been cases of political violence in no less than seven states, with the latest in Lagos, where several supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) were injured after suspected political thugs disrupted a town hall meeting organised on Thursday by the party for its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso. There was also an incident in Zamfara State during an All Progressives Congress (APC) primary. INEC will obey court verdict on Atiku’s eligibility – Amupitan How 4 UNN students died after graduation party Other states that recorded violence within the period included Edo, Delta, Gombe and Cross River states. The incidents have been more frequent this year, with states like Katsina, Kebbi, Enugu, Ekiti, Ondo, Ebonyi, Osun and Nasarawa states all experiencing various forms of political violence. Prominent political actors have also threatened voters in ways that raised concerns over free, fair and credible polls in 2027. The National Peace Committee revealed recently that reports spanning August 19 to October 27 documented 109 breaches of the National Peace Accord across 26 states and the Federal Capital Territory. It also observed that political violence and thuggery led the violations with 33 incidents, closely followed by 29 cases of misinformation and disinformation and identified Kaduna, Edo, and Enugu as serious flashpoints for electoral violence. The European Union (EU) also expressed concern over reports of election-related violence, hate speech and political intimidation ahead of Nigeria’s general elections. EU Ambassador and Head of Delegation to Nigeria and ECOWAS, Gautier Mignot, noted that these threats undermined democratic progress and discouraged citizens from participating freely in the electoral process.
